title: Assyrian Egypt
capsule: "Assyrian Egypt" denotes the roughly fifteen years during which the Neo-Assyrian Empire claimed suzerainty over Egypt, principally Lower Egypt and the Nile Delta. Esarhaddon invaded and captured Memphis in 671 BC, driving out the Kushite pharaoh Taharqa and seizing his family, and after repeated Kushite counter-attacks Ashurbanipal sacked Thebes in 663 BC. The Assyrians ruled indirectly through Egyptian vassal princes, most notably Necho I and his son Psamtik I of Sais; Psamtik gradually consolidated power and, exploiting Assyria's distraction elsewhere, reunified Egypt and ended Assyrian control by about 656 BC, founding the Twenty-sixth (Saite) Dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Assyrian control of Egypt is documented in royal annals (prisms of Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal) and Egyptian administrative papyri; the territorial footprint is well established for Lower Egypt and the Nile Delta but conjectural for Upper Egypt south of Thebes.
